headline: Barn Owls Nest in Manhattan Water Tower, a First for Modern History
meta_description: A family of barn owls has nested in a water tower near Central Park in what experts believe is the first documented nest in Manhattan's modern history.
summary_short: A family of barn owls has become Manhattan's newest celebrities after nesting in a water tower near Central Park, marking a historic moment for the borough.
body:
A family of barn owls has become Manhattan's newest celebrities after nesting in a water tower near Central Park—what experts believe is the first documented nest in the borough's modern history.

The sighting marks an unexpected return of the species to one of the world's most densely populated urban centers. Barn owls, typically associated with rural farmland and open countryside, have historically been absent from Manhattan's landscape. The presence of a breeding family in a water tower near Central Park suggests that urban wildlife is finding unexpected refuge in the city's infrastructure.

This development offers a rare window into how wildlife adapts to human environments and raises questions about the hidden ecosystems thriving in plain sight across the city.
